html:
An oral epic of the Mande peoples that tells the life of Sundiata Keita, the crippled prince who rose to defeat the sorcerer king Sumanguru and founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century.

It has been passed down for centuries by griots, hereditary bards and keepers of history, such as the Kouyate family, and is still performed with the kora and balafon in Mali, Guinea, Senegal and the Gambia. Versions differ by region and teller. The Guinean historian D. T. Niane published a famous prose version in 1960, and the story has inspired novels, plays and films. It is a main source, with Arab writers, for the history of Mali. See also the Kouroukan Fouga.
sum: An oral epic of the Mande peoples that tells the life of Sundiata Keita, the crippled prince who rose to defeat the sorcerer king Sumanguru and founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century.
